articles.summary: Writer's "Recalling Too Well" paper says memory systems amplify sycophancy. Its own data traces the amplification to two design decisions — one in Writer's experiment itself, one in a competitor's memory product.
articles.title: Sycophancy is a design choice

articles.summary: Agent memory has to refresh every turn, but putting it in the system prompt breaks prompt caching and re-bills the whole conversation each turn. Here is the one-message fix, and the token savings it led to in an experiment.
articles.title: Agent memory placement can cut your token bill up to 2x

articles.summary: Today we're announcing Smart Context Assembly, an upgrade to how Zep's default Context Block is built: higher accuracy from fewer tokens, with no code changes.
articles.title: Smart Context Assembly: Fewer Tokens, Better Quality

articles.summary: A production agent is a long-running, concurrent, I/O-bound process that spends most of its time waiting on a model, a tool, or a human. That shape fits Go's runtime. This post explains why, surveys the Go framework options, and shows how to build an agent without one.
articles.title: Building Agents in Go Without a Framework

articles.summary: Zep's Batch API loads large datasets into agent memory faster, in batches up to 50,000 items, with a progress dashboard and no impact on real-time ingestion.
articles.title: The Batch API: Load Large Datasets into Agent Memory

articles.summary: Your team's agents are split across surfaces: the desktop assistant, the coding tool, the agents you build in-house. Each keeps its own memory or none at all. The Memory MCP Server puts them on one governed user graph, gated by your enterprise single sign-on.
articles.title: Unified agent memory in any MCP client

articles.summary: Some of the most capable agents in production keep their memory in plain markdown files, and for a single agent and a single user it is hard to beat. The pattern breaks in predictable places: at scale, as facts change and errors compound, and under concurrent agents.
articles.title: Markdown is not agent memory
